content.purpose: Pass a spaced filename to a command as one argument.
content.mentalModel: The shell normally splits unquoted whitespace into argument boundaries. Quotes or backslash escapes suppress that split.

demonstration.explanation: This small example isolates the main idea behind file names with spaces.

tasks.instruction: Create an empty file named monthly report.txt inside /home/student/lab. The space must be part of the filename.
hints: The shell must receive the whole path as one argument.
Wrap the path in quotes or escape the space with a backslash.
Check with ls -l before assuming two visible words mean two files.
